steps.what: Monitor and operate plant communications systems such as mobile radios

tasks.design: The manager listens, clarifies and responds through the existing communications system. Existing contact information in {DOCS} supports communication without replacing live acknowledgement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Radio messages depend on context, timing and confirmation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communications equipment supports the task; no validated automatic operator is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding ambiguous or urgent traffic in noisy conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The manager clarifies intent and coordinates the appropriate response.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live plant radio operation remains human; ordinary radio transmission runtime is not removable labour.

assumptions: Boundary is radio monitoring and operation, excluding the physical work discussed over radio.
Plant staff produce messages during s1 and the manager confirms their meaning there; no free structured instruction feed is assumed.
Check native communications functions first; existing runtime earns no labour saving. Zero incremental upkeep because no new system is added.
research_questions: Which messages require clarification before the manager responds?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. All live communication remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile and record biomass operational data

steps.what: Collect operational data and verify observations for the plant log
Compile operational data into the required forms or log book fields
Check and record the final operational log entry

tasks.design: Configure an electronic log in {OPS_SYSTEM} to populate the required fields from the manager's verified entry pack. The manager checks values, context and corrections before saving the final entry; required physical observation is retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified readings and observations can be copied repeatedly into paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native electronic forms can reuse captured values with source references and a correction trail.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a bad reading or an observation that needs explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The manager checks whether the record faithfully represents plant events.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated transcription, with observation and log accountability unchanged.

reach.task: Agree operational log definitions and correction handling

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native electronic logs can reuse verified fields, but local acceptance of electronic records and the transcription baseline must be confirmed.

assumptions: Boundary is operational log compilation, excluding live condition monitoring in task 15479 and inspection or maintenance execution. An observation has one labour owner in roll-ups.

Existing instruments and operators produce readings and observations. In s1 the manager verifies and captures timestamp, plant/equipment ID, measured value, unit, source reference, observation text, author and correction reason when relevant; the full 45% remains and no extra operator data-entry work is assumed.

The log administrator verifies field mappings and allowed units with 3 other-role hours per 100 focal baseline hours of ongoing upkeep. Missing fields or disputed readings return to manual entry and checking; no automatically inferred operating-status code is assumed.

Test native electronic forms first and confirm electronic records meet local requirements. If paper is mandatory or copying is already automated, retain the existing process with zero new saving. Existing runtime earns no labour saving.
Seven incremental focal hours cover log-template changes, extra entry exceptions and correction audits.
unknowns: Actual repeated transcription time and source completeness
research_questions: Can an electronic log reproduce a checked paper entry while preserving provenance and corrections?

incremental.description: Template changes, extra exceptions and correction audits

approvals.approved_version: Exact log entry, timestamp, equipment ID, values, units, observation text and source references checked in s3; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+20=65; gross 35%, net 28% after 7 focal upkeep. Range covers mandatory paper or existing automation with no new saving through 19 points of duplicate transcription removed minus 7 upkeep. Capture and review remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Monitor operating status by observing control system parameters, gauges and indicators

tasks.design: The manager observes existing process-control displays {OTHER} and interprets operating status. Existing automatic regulation continues without being counted as newly saved manager time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operating status depends on the meaning and reliability of several signals.
tasks.enabler_now: Current displays support assessment without demonstrating that oversight can be removed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising sensor faults and conflicting indications.
tasks.human_edge: The manager understands the plant context and escalates uncertainty.

reach.task: Coordinate investigation of conflicting operating signals

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing control-system runtime is not human labour; this design retains operating-status interpretation.

assumptions: Boundary is live status monitoring, excluding log transcription in task 15466 and corrective execution.
OTHER means plant process-control system. Existing instruments produce readings; the manager interprets them during s1. No free structured plant-safe flag or new predictive model is assumed.
Test existing native displays first. Zero incremental upkeep because no new automation is introduced; current controller runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Existing monitoring requirements and display configuration
research_questions: Which abnormal conditions need manager interpretation despite existing alarms?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; net 0%. Existing alarms and regulation do not remove the stated human monitoring step.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Electronic logs can reduce duplicate transcription while communications and live operating judgement stay human.
reach: Coordinate traceable operational entries with the plant records owner.
role.ambitious_version: Reliable plant records with observed conditions and human monitoring time fully counted.
